title: The Mould That Saved Lives
paragraphs: In nineteen twenty eight, a scientist named Alexander Fleming came back to his laboratory after a holiday. He saw something strange in one of his dishes. Fleming was very curious, so he looked at the dish carefully. A mould was growing there, and the bacteria around it were dying.

Fleming wrote about his discovery, but he did not turn it into a medicine. Years later, two other scientists, Howard Florey and Ernst Chain, worked with their team to make penicillin strong and safe enough for patients. Their work began to save many lives in the nineteen forties.

In nineteen forty five, Fleming, Florey and Chain shared the Nobel Prize for this discovery. Today, penicillin and similar medicines are called antibiotics, and they treat many infections. So a small mould in a dish changed modern medicine. Doctors still use these medicines in hospitals all over the world.
